title: Maize — Irrigation Scheduling and Water Management
content:
MAIZE IRRIGATION MANAGEMENT:

CRITICAL IRRIGATION STAGES:
1. Germination (0-7 DAS): Pre-sowing irrigation essential for uniform germination.
2. Knee-high stage (25-30 DAS): Critical for vegetative establishment.
3. Tasseling and Silking (50-60 DAS): MOST CRITICAL — even 2-3 days of water stress causes 20-30% yield loss (poor pollination/fertilization).
4. Grain filling (70-80 DAS): Important for grain weight.
5. Maturity (90+ DAS): Reduce water 2 weeks before harvest.

IRRIGATION INTERVALS:
- Kharif (rainfed): Supplement irrigation at critical stages if >15 day rainfall gap.
- Rabi/Summer: Irrigate every 7-10 days.
- Total water requirement: 500-600 mm.

IMPORTANT:
- Maize is VERY SENSITIVE to waterlogging. Excess water for >48h causes yellowing and root damage.
- Ensure proper drainage in ridges-and-furrows system.
- Avoid flat sowing in heavy soils — always use ridge-furrow.

IRRIGATION METHODS:
- Furrow irrigation: Preferred for ridged maize — 70-80 mm per irrigation.
- Drip irrigation: Saves 40-50% water. Use 16 LPH emitters at 60 cm spacing.
- Sprinkler: Effective for germination and early stages.

PRE-SOWING IRRIGATION:
- For rabi season, pre-sowing irrigation is mandatory to ensure good germination in dry soil.
- Irrigate 5-7 days before sowing.
